recommendation: Use all 4 banked free transfers on the model's optimum: Dubravka -> Raya, Rogers + Tzolis -> Mbeumo + Tavernier, Isak -> Thiago. No hit. Do not wildcard.
reasoning: Model puts this at +18.22 xP over six gameweeks against holding, all free. The 5-transfer plan that adds Palmer scores +19.83 raw but -4 for the hit, so +15.83 net — Palmer costs about 2.4 xP versus this plan. Wildcard is the highest raw at +23.03 but only about +4.8 over simply spending the free transfers, which is a weak case for burning a chip in a single gameweek with no double. Free Hit is +6.74 for one week and clearly not worth it.
case_against: The model sells Rogers, who has the strongest creator consensus in the squad (0.83 weighted, 44 mentions, all 4 creators) and 4.9 xP this week at home to Hull. It also buys Tavernier on only 3 mentions from 2 creators. All four creators independently want Palmer and captain him or Joao Pedro; the model never buys Palmer inside the free-transfer budget because his six-week xP (20.2) is below Tavernier (21.2) and Mbeumo (20.5) at a much higher price. There is no calibrated robustness margin yet, so a 2.4 xP gap over six gameweeks is not established as real. Four transfers is also heavy squad churn on an unvalidated model.

recommendation: Reconsider the wildcard. My earlier 'hold it' call understated it and I no longer stand behind that reasoning.
reasoning: Two errors in the original comparison. First, I read the ranking as the whole answer, but decisions.py deliberately keeps transfer stock out of the ranking: the wildcard scores +30.20 at a ten-week horizon AND leaves 5 free transfers, while the best four-transfer plan scores +24.21 and leaves 1. Four preserved transfers are worth several more points on top of the ~6 point gap. Second, I measured over six gameweeks when the chip's benefit runs to GW19: the edge grows from +4.81 at six weeks to +5.63 at eight and +5.99 at ten. Structurally, the chip expires after GW19, all four original creators say a first-half double gameweek is very unlikely, and the squad has six weak spots against four free transfers - which is the condition a wildcard exists for. The wildcard squad also buys Palmer and Saka, which no free-transfer plan can afford.
case_against: A wildcard is irreversible and the model has never been scored. A roughly 12 point edge spread over 15 gameweeks is about 0.8 per week, which no measured robustness margin supports; making four reversible free transfers keeps the option open at a cost that is inside noise. The wildcard also sells Rogers, which Joe has ruled out - under his constraints it is +21.39 rather than +23.03, still ahead of +16.06 for four free transfers but by less. Several creators activating chips in the same week is not independent evidence: they publish chip-reveal content for a living.

recommendation: TAKEN: 3 transfers, no hit. OUT Palestra, Gibbs-White, Tzolis. IN Hall, Palmer, Tavernier. Banks 2 free transfers and £0.5m. No chip.
reasoning: Model puts this at +12.87 xP over six gameweeks against holding. Palestra is the clean sale: flagged doubtful, zero minutes all season, worst value in the squad at 1.92 points per million, price at -80% of a fall, and not one mention across 868 findings from seven creators. Tzolis is the second: lowest sustained projection in the squad at 10.8 over six, only a 61 percent chance of 60-plus minutes after being hooked at half time in GW2, and two assists produced from 0.35 expected assists and 0.19 expected goals in three games - both returns are overperformance on almost no underlying threat, and his GW3 90 minutes carried exactly zero xG. Palmer is the strongest expert signal in the corpus: 99 mentions from all seven creators at 0.97 consensus, the highest single-gameweek projection in the game at 6.07, Chelsea's penalty taker, at home to Hull whose three clean sheets mask over five expected goals conceded. Tavernier is the model's own best six-week asset at 21.2 for 6.0m, carried by consistent DefCon returns of 8, 11 and 9. Hall has five creators at 0.58, the best fixture run of any target at an average FDR of 2.7 over GW4-9, and played 90 with an assist in Newcastle's Carabao Cup tie.
case_against: Gibbs-White is sold as funding, not on merit, and Joe was sad to let him go. Model signal 0.96, third-best six-week projection among his midfielders at 18.3, positive consensus of 0.50 across four creators, Nottingham Forest's penalty AND set-piece taker, and a good run ahead in Aston Villa away, Coventry at home and Crystal Palace away. He is only leaving because Palmer costs 9.6m and he was the most expensive dispensable asset. The alternative funding was B.Fernandes, rejected because he is the model's highest six-week total in the game at 24.6 and selling him would force the captaincy to move anyway. Tavernier is also the single biggest model-versus-room disagreement in the corpus - the model's top pick on only 4 mentions from 3 creators, so either an edge or the model being wrong. There is still no calibrated robustness margin, so none of these gaps are established as real.
runner_up: 2 transfers only: Palestra and Tzolis out, banking 3 FT and £2.2m to see Wednesday's Carabao minutes first

recommendation: TAKEN: captain Palmer, vice B.Fernandes. Supersedes the earlier B.Fernandes recommendation.
reasoning: Palmer projects 6.07 for GW4 against Bruno's 5.53, and the captaincy moves with the transfer. Chelsea host Hull at fixture difficulty 2; Palmer is the penalty taker; Planet FPL's Chelsea correspondent Gary Mantle explicitly prefers him to João Pedro because Hull's back three squeezes the deep space João Pedro wants; and Focal argues the market misprices him because Hull's three clean sheets mask conceding over five expected goals. Bruno drops to vice on the hardest fixture any owned player faces, Man City at difficulty 4.
case_against: Bruno remains the model's highest six-week total in the game at 24.6 and was its captain in every projected gameweek before this transfer. BigManBakar gates his own Triple Captain on Palmer's midweek League Cup minutes - a substitute around 60 is a green light, over 80 a red flag - and that fixture had not been played when this was decided. Danny McDonald of Planet FPL dissents and backs Isak instead. Market flow is also one-sided: Bruno is leaving at -550 net transfers per hour from 45.8 percent ownership, which is the crowd behaviour that creates value rather than destroys it.
runner_up: B.Fernandes at home to Man City

recommendation: TAKEN: no chip. Wildcard, Free Hit, Bench Boost and Triple Captain all held.
reasoning: Joe's own test settled it: a wildcard is a substitute for paying hits, and its value is highest when the number of changes wanted exceeds the transfers available. He wanted three and had four. The wildcard's edge over spending free transfers is about 0.6 to 0.8 xP per week and shrinking with horizon, and it is still available for fifteen gameweeks. Lateriser independently reached the same conclusion, taking a Free Hit specifically so he could delay his wildcard two to three weeks and build it properly.
case_against: The wildcard scores highest in raw terms and also preserves five free transfers against one, which decisions.py deliberately keeps outside the ranking - so the ranking understates it. It is the only route that affords both Palmer and Saka. The chip expires after GW19 and all creators say a first-half double gameweek is unlikely, so holding for a perfect window may mean spending it in an ordinary gameweek later anyway.

recommendation: Palmer captaincy gate RESOLVED in favour: he came on at half-time in the Carabao Cup against Leeds and scored twice in two minutes, one a penalty.
reasoning: The gw4-6 entry recorded that the midweek cup fixture had not been played when the captaincy was decided. It had - the error was mine, Joe had already told me the game happened. BigManBakar's stated gate was a substitute around 60 minutes as a green light and over 80 as a red flag; Palmer played roughly 45 as a second-half substitute, so he is fresher than the green-light case. He also took and converted a penalty, which is the specific reason Planet FPL's Chelsea correspondent Gary Mantle gave for preferring him to João Pedro as captain. Chelsea won 6-3.
case_against: Cup form is not league form and the opposition was Leeds in a third-round tie. Cup goals score no FPL points and this must not touch the projection - Palmer's 6.07 xP is unchanged. A half-time introduction also means the manager rested him for a reason, which cuts both ways: fresh for Saturday, but it says nothing about whether he starts. Source is a match report, not the FPL API, which records league rounds only.

recommendation: SUPERSEDES gw4-5. Final: OUT Palestra, Tzolis, Isak. IN Tarkowski, Palmer, Barry. 3 transfers, no hit, no chip. Captain Palmer, vice B.Fernandes. Banks 2 free transfers.
reasoning: Changed from the earlier Hall/Palmer/Tavernier plan for three reasons Joe gave. First, Tavernier is a player he wants but not yet: the model's case for him is the six-week total of 21.2, and his GW5-6 run is Liverpool at home then Chelsea away, so the plan is to target him on a GW6 wildcard instead of paying a transfer for him now. Second, this keeps Gibbs-White, whom the earlier plan sold purely as funding and Joe was sad to lose - Harry bought him this week, he is Forest's penalty and set-piece taker, and four creators are positive. Third, Isak goes instead as the rotation risk: 52.6 expected minutes, the lowest of any starting forward, FPLtips saw him subbed at 60 for Champions League rotation, and Let's Talk FPL read the buying frenzy as a reaction to his two goals rather than to his role. Barry replaces him at 5.6m. Palmer is the captain on near-unanimous evidence: 99 mentions from all seven creators, penalty taker, at home to Hull, and he came on at half-time in the Carabao Cup to score twice including a penalty, so he is fresh and confirmed to start.
case_against: Joe took Tarkowski over Hall against my recommendation. Over GW4-5 - the window that matters if he wildcards at GW6 - they are 0.12 points apart, and Tarkowski costs 0.9m more. Tarkowski's entire edge is GW6 (4.04 vs 3.44), the gameweek a wildcard would erase. Tarkowski also has zero mentions across 1,013 findings; Hall has five creators at 0.58 consensus and played 90 in the Carabao Cup with an assist. If the wildcard does land in GW6, this is 0.9m spent for almost nothing. Separately, Calvert-Lewin was 0.2 behind Barry with 75 expected minutes to Barry's 63 and the strongest creator backing in the corpus at 0.86 from six creators. And there is still no calibrated robustness margin, so none of these gaps are established.
runner_up: Hall instead of Tarkowski, banking 2.0m rather than 1.1m
